Let d be an integer that is not divisible√by n-th powers of primes, let xn − d
be an irreducible polynomial over Q, let θ = n d, and let K = Q(θ) be the radical
extension of degree n of the field Q. The multiplicative group K ∗ of the field K is
canonically embedded into the group AutQ (K) of all invertible Q-linear mappings of
the Q-space K; let T be the image of K ∗ under this embedding. In the natural basis
1, θ, θ2 , . . . , θn−1 of the Q-space K the group AutQ (K) corresponds to G = GL(n, Q),
and the subgroup T to a subgroup T (d) (unsplit maximal torus). Every subgroup H
of G containing T (d) and some one-dimensional transformation is rich in elementary
transvections (V. A. Koibaev, St. Petersbg. Math. J., 21, no. 5 (2010), 731–742)
and thus defines a net σ = σ(H) (V. A. Koibaev, A. V. Shilov, J. Math. Sci. New
York 171, no. 3 (2010), 380–385). Let E(σ) denote the subgroup generated by all
transvections in the net group G(σ). Is it true that H ⩽ NG (E(σ))?
    This inclusion was proved in the case n = 2 (V. A. Koibaev, Dokl. Math., 41, no. 3
(1990), 414–416).                                                           V. A. Koibaev
